text: Recent visitor feedback for the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library highlights issues with signage and accessibility, particularly for those needing handicap parking and shuttle service from the lot to the entrance. Several reviews criticize the use of AI in exhibits, describing it as poorly executed and detracting from the experience. Some visitors were frustrated by timed entry policies and wait times, including the need to purchase tickets in advance and delays in gaining entry. Food options in the café received negative comments, and a few noted crowding and limited seating. Positive remarks focused on the building’s architecture and interactive exhibits, but these did not fully offset concerns raised.

windows.60: Visitors have noted issues with signage and accessibility, particularly the lack of clear directions to handicap parking and limited shuttle service from the parking area to the entrance. Several reviews criticized the use of AI in exhibits, describing it as poorly executed or distracting, and some expressed disappointment with the number of replica items on display. Timed entry and ticketing policies caused frustration for some guests who were unable to enter promptly. Food options in the café received negative comments, and a few visitors mentioned crowding and wait times as detracting from their experience. Overall, the library’s architecture and interactive exhibits remain well-regarded, but improvements in accessibility, exhibit technology, and visitor flow could enhance satisfaction.
